title: Specialisation and the benefits of trade

match.reason: The bank point e-special teaches the division of labour and the functions of money and financial markets, not the benefits of trade between countries in raising production, incomes and choice, so it is a related but different idea.

draft.title: Specialisation and the benefits of trade
card: Specialisation is when a country puts its resources into making the goods and services it does best. It then makes a lot of them.
Trade lets a country do this. It can sell what it makes in large amounts and buy the other things it needs from other countries.
Specialising and trading can raise total production. More output can raise incomes, and buyers get a wider choice of goods and services.
Trade can also build ties between countries, because they come to rely on each other for goods, services and customers.
draft.remember: Trade lets countries specialise, which can lift output, incomes and choice.

a.q: What does it mean for a country to specialise?
opts: It focuses its resources on what it does best
It makes a little of every good its people use
It buys all its goods from other countries
It stops selling goods to other countries
a.why: Specialisation means putting resources into the goods and services a country does best. Making a little of everything is the opposite, because resources are spread thinly instead of focused.
a.clue: Think about where the country puts its resources.

b.q: Two neighbouring countries each stop making everything and focus on what they do best. They then trade with each other. What is the most likely result?
opts: Total production rises and people have more choice
Total production falls because each makes fewer goods
Each country makes more types of goods than before
The countries become less tied to each other
b.why: Each country makes a lot of what it does best, so total production can rise. Trade then gives people goods they no longer make. Production does not fall just because each country makes fewer types of goods, since it makes much more of the ones it focuses on.
b.clue: Each country makes fewer types of goods but more of each one.

a.best: It focuses its resources on what it does best

b.best: Total production rises and people have more choice
